# 01b — Audit of the Google Earth Engine raster pipeline (product A)

*Generated by `make audit-gee` (`src/aparri/audit_gee.py`). Read-only; all numbers are computed from the files in `data/raw/gee_outputs/`. Vocabulary: **NSM** = metres moved between 1990 and 2025; **EPR** = NSM ÷ 35 yr (m/yr, negative = erosion); a **pixel** is a Landsat-grid cell of 28.5 × 29.8 m = 0.0850 ha.*

## Executive summary (≤12 lines)

1. The script (`Code.docx`) is a plain, readable Landsat/NDWI workflow, and its **risk rule matches the thesis thresholds** (verified pixel by pixel: 116,183 of 116,183 risk-raster pixels equal the rule applied to the EPR raster).
2. But it measures **land↔water change between 1990 and 2025 only**; 2000/2010/2020 never enter any rate, and NSM is a **pixel-distance approximation** (the script says so itself).
3. **"Accretion" is an artefact:** 31,240 accretion pixels (2,654 ha) vs 2,052 erosion pixels (174 ha) = **15×**; **96 % of the accretion pixels lie in the open sea** and 98% are > 150 m from any mapped shoreline.
4. **The years are not comparable:** edge pixels per year 2,589, 2,711, 2,367, 7,433, 20,321; in 2025 83% of them are in open water (0 % in 1990–2010). 2025 has **7.8×** the edge pixels of 1990.
5. **No High pixel is on the open coast:** of 88 High pixels, 0 are near an open-coast line and 82 are near river/estuary banks (Cagayan River mouth). Medium: 130 open-coast, 223 river/estuary.
6. **Barangay table = 1 km circles around single points** (confirmed: reproduced within ≈ 1–5 %). `Low_Risk_ha` ≈ circle area (314 ha) for 4 of 8 rows; **Paddaya, Bulala Sur** have no EPR (point outside the box); Dodan is clipped to 34 ha.
7. Recomputed with the **official polygons**, the raster has **1.44 ha of High inside the eight polygons** (+500 m tolerance: 3.65 ha, in Linao, Maura); Bulala Sur is outside the raster and Paddaya is 1.9 % covered.
8. **Verdict:** the raster pipeline is *usable as a screening hint*, **not** as the source of Table 4.2, Fig. 4.2 or any rate (verdict table §6).
9. **Decisions needed** (Decision Gates #1–#4): who wrote/ran the script and whether the thesis will describe it as the method; whether anything from the 1 km statistics reached the thesis; which shoreline set is primary (Phase 3B comparison); and whether Landsat may be re-fetched (Phase 3C). Phase 3C **cannot run in this sandbox** (Landsat catalogues unreachable, no Earth Engine login) — see `docs/decisions.md` D-04.

---

## 1. Method card (what the script does, in plain English)

| Step | What the script does | Script section | Problem / caution |
|---|---|---|---|
| Area | One rectangle: lon 121.58–121.72, lat 18.33–18.39 | §1 | Misses Bulala Sur (lon 121.566) and Paddaya (lat 18.310); clips Dodan (lat 18.324) |
| Sensors | ≤ 2012: Landsat 4 + 5 + 7; 2013–2020: Landsat 8; 2021+: Landsat 8 + 9. Collection 2 Level-2 surface reflectance | §3, §6 | 1990 relies on Landsat 4/5 only; Landsat 7 (used for 2000 and 2010) has the scan-line-corrector gaps after May 2003 |
| Composite | For each calendar year: **median** of all scenes (Jan–Dec, every season and tide) | §6 | Mixes wet/dry season, tide, river stage; image counts are printed but were never saved; acquisition dates are not recorded |
| Cloud mask | QA_PIXEL bits: fill (bit 1 dilated cloud), cloud (3), shadow (4); cirrus (2) for Landsat 8/9 | §4–5 | Only these flags; no water-confidence or glint handling |
| Water index | NDWI = (Green − NIR)/(Green + NIR) **> 0**, fixed threshold | §7–8 | One global threshold for all years and sensors; no calibration; masked pixels are later set to 0 (= land) |
| "Shoreline" | Pixels where a 3×3 maximum differs from the 3×3 minimum of the water mask | §11 | An **edge band** about 2 pixels thick (≈ 60 m), not a line; any speckle produces "shoreline" |
| Change | Erosion = land in 1990 and water in 2025; accretion = water in 1990 and land in 2025 | §13–15 | Only two years; a cloud hole or a mask error in either year becomes "change" |
| NSM | Distance to the nearest 1990 edge pixel (erosion, negative) or 2025 edge pixel (accretion, positive), × 30 | §17–18 | "A raster-distance approximation… a transect-based NSM is preferable" (script's own note); × 30 ignores the real 28.5/29.8 m pixel; distance search capped at 256 px |
| EPR | NSM ÷ 35 | §19 | Every non-zero value is a pixel multiple (smallest 0.857 = 30/35) |
| Risk | 1 Low (default, includes accretion, stable land **and open sea**); 2 Medium if EPR<0 and 2 ≤ \|EPR\| ≤ 5; 3 High if EPR<0 and \|EPR\| > 5 | §22–24 | Matches Table 3.1 thresholds (inclusive 2 and 5) |
| Barangays | 8 **points** → 1 km radius circles; mean/min/max, hectares per class | §28–31 | Script: "temporary… replace with official boundaries" |
| Exports | CSV, SHP, 9 GeoTIFFs, EPSG:4326, 30 m | §32–38 | No metadata; vector shorelines and risk polygons are **not** exported by this script |

**Not recorded anywhere:** image count and acquisition dates per year, seasons, tide state, cloud fraction, NDWI values, who ran it and when.

## 2. Raster audit

| file | crs | width | height | dtype | distinct_values | min | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Aparri_EPR_1990_2025.tif | EPSG:4326 | 521 | 223 | float32 | 128 | -82.04 | 14.80 |
| Aparri_Erosion_Accretion_1990_2025.tif | EPSG:4326 | 521 | 223 | uint8 | 3 | 0.00 | 2.00 |
| Aparri_Erosion_Risk_1990_2025.tif | EPSG:4326 | 521 | 223 | uint8 | 3 | 1.00 | 3.00 |
| Aparri_NSM_1990_2025.tif | EPSG:4326 | 521 | 223 | float32 | 128 | -2,871.24 | 517.88 |
| Aparri_Shoreline_1990.tif | EPSG:4326 | 521 | 223 | uint8 | 2 | 0.00 | 1.00 |
| Aparri_Shoreline_2000.tif | EPSG:4326 | 521 | 223 | uint8 | 2 | 0.00 | 1.00 |
| Aparri_Shoreline_2010.tif | EPSG:4326 | 521 | 223 | uint8 | 2 | 0.00 | 1.00 |
| Aparri_Shoreline_2020.tif | EPSG:4326 | 521 | 223 | uint8 | 2 | 0.00 | 1.00 |
| Aparri_Shoreline_2025.tif | EPSG:4326 | 521 | 223 | uint8 | 2 | 0.00 | 1.00 |

* CRS EPSG:4326 for all; 521 × 223 px; **28.48 m (E–W) × 29.83 m (N–S)** at this latitude — pixels are not square, so `distance × 30` is only an approximation. Extent x 121.5798–121.7202, y 18.3299–18.3900 (the requested box, snapped to the pixel grid). No NoData value is set.
* **Class legend** (not documented in the files; inferred from the script §14–15 and §37, then tested): `Erosion_Accretion` 0 = none, **1 = erosion**, **2 = accretion**; `Erosion_Risk` 1 Low, 2 Medium, 3 High. Tests: code 0 ⇒ NSM = 0 for all 82,891 pixels: True; erosion pixels have NSM ≤ 0: True (733 are exactly 0 – they sit on the 1990 edge itself); accretion pixels NSM ≥ 0: True; EPR = NSM/35 everywhere: True; risk raster = rule(EPR): True. **Legend CONFIRMED (high certainty).**
* Pixel counts / hectares: none 82,891 (7,042 ha) · erosion 2,052 (174 ha) · accretion 31,240 (2,654 ha); risk Low 115,708 (9,831 ha) · Medium 387 (32.9 ha) · High 88 (7.5 ha).
* **Quantisation:** 128 distinct EPR values; 100% of non-zero NSM satisfy (NSM/30)² = integer, i.e. NSM = 30·√(a²+b²) for whole-pixel offsets (a, b). Smallest |NSM| = 30 m, smallest |EPR| = 0.8571 = 30/35 = 0.8571. **Resolution of the method is one pixel (≈ 30 m ≈ 0.86 m/yr); the Low/Medium boundary (2 m/yr) is only 2.3 pixels.**
* **Extreme values** (EPR < −14 m/yr): 4 pixels, all along the bottom edge of the box at lon ≈ 121.588–121.603, lat ≈ 18.332–18.354 (zone: land). They are artefacts of the box edge / the 256-pixel distance cap (NSM down to -2,871 m). Full list: `outputs/tables/gee_extreme_epr_pixels.csv`.

### Why is 2025 about 8× noisier than 1990?

| year | edge_pixels | components | median_component_px | components_le_5px | largest_component_px | share_open_coast | share_sea | share_inner_water | share_land |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,990.00 | 2,589.00 | 28.00 | 8.00 | 12.00 | 1,016.00 | 0.41 | 0.00 | 0.07 | 0.52 |
| 2,000.00 | 2,711.00 | 22.00 | 15.00 | 7.00 | 1,108.00 | 0.37 | 0.00 | 0.05 | 0.59 |
| 2,010.00 | 2,367.00 | 8.00 | 50.00 | 1.00 | 1,076.00 | 0.41 | 0.00 | 0.04 | 0.55 |
| 2,020.00 | 7,433.00 | 78.00 | 11.00 | 28.00 | 1,744.00 | 0.18 | 0.61 | 0.00 | 0.21 |
| 2,025.00 | 20,321.00 | 165.00 | 8.00 | 81.00 | 7,725.00 | 0.09 | 0.83 | 0.00 | 0.08 |

* Edge pixels grow from 2,589 (1990) to **20,321** (2025); the number of separate pieces from 28 to 165, and 83% of the 2025 edge pixels (and 61% of 2020's) lie in the **open sea** where there is no shoreline, against 0 % in 1990, 2000 and 2010. See `outputs/maps/gee_edge_noise_by_year.png`.
* **What is certain:** the 2020 and 2025 water masks break up over open water. **What is not certain (HYPOTHESIS):** the cause. Candidates: a fixed NDWI > 0 threshold behaving differently on Landsat 8/9 than on 4/5/7 over turbid sea water (river sediment plume, glint), different numbers of scenes per year, or cloud holes set to land. The NDWI values were never exported, so this cannot be tested from the files.

## 3. Plausibility tests

Zones: *open coast* = within 350 m of the sea-facing outline of all legacy shorelines (`scope.py`); *sea* = beyond it; the rest lies inside the municipal polygons (which include the Cagayan River) or outside them in the river mouth. "Nearest legacy line" uses only the supplied vector lines (product B), 150 m band.

| measure | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| set | Risk High (3) | Risk Medium (2) | Erosion pixels (code 1) | Accretion pixels (code 2) |
| pixels | 88 | 387 | 2052 | 31240 |
| ha | 7.5 | 32.9 | 174.3 | 2,654.1 |
| open_coast_px | 3 | 134 | 989 | 738 |
| open_coast_pct | 3.4 | 34.6 | 48.2 | 2.4 |
| sea_px | 0 | 0 | 0 | 29968 |
| sea_pct | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 95.9 |
| inner_water_px | 19 | 31 | 169 | 0 |
| inner_water_pct | 21.6 | 8.0 | 8.2 | 0.0 |
| land_px | 66 | 222 | 894 | 534 |
| land_pct | 75.0 | 57.4 | 43.6 | 1.7 |
| line_n | 88 | 387 | 2052 | 31240 |
| line_near_open_coast_line | 0 | 130 | 936 | 165 |
| line_near_river_estuary_line | 82 | 223 | 943 | 508 |
| line_no_mapped_shoreline_within_band | 6 | 34 | 173 | 30567 |

* (a) **Where are the 88 High and 387 Medium pixels?** High: 0 near the open coast, **82 near river/estuary banks**, 6 near no mapped shoreline. Medium: 130 / 223 / 34. See `outputs/maps/gee_high_medium_pixels.png`.
* (b) **Are they on the open coast, river mouth, ponds?** Mostly the Cagayan River mouth (Linao spit, sandbars, banks); fishponds/inland water cannot be separated without the NDWI image.
* (c) **Does NDWI>0 create inland "shorelines"?** Yes, by construction: any water body (river, pond, paddy) has an edge. 52% of 1990 edge pixels are inside municipal polygons away from the open coast. The script never separates "coast" from "inland water".
* (d) **Accretion 15× erosion — physical or artefact?** Artefact: **95.9 % of accretion pixels are in the open sea** (zone *sea*), 97.8% are > 150 m from any mapped shoreline. Water in 1990, "land" in 2025, over the sea: this is the 2025 mask failing. If the sea block is discarded, accretion falls from 2,654 ha to ≈ 108 ha (vs erosion 174 ha). `outputs/maps/gee_zones_and_change.png`.

## 5. Sensitivity of the raster method

Only the binary edge masks and the derived rasters were exported — **no NDWI image**. A threshold sweep (−0.1/0/+0.1) is therefore impossible from the files. What Phase 3C would need: (i) the per-year NDWI (or MNDWI/AWEI) composites saved as rasters, (ii) the list of scenes used (id, date, sensor, cloud %), (iii) a per-composite threshold (Otsu) instead of 0, (iv) a seasonal window and a tide estimate, (v) a sub-pixel contour. `src/aparri/landsat.py` and `scripts/gee_v2.js` implement this; it **was not run** here (no network route to Landsat, no Earth Engine login).

## 6. Verdict: which thesis claims depend on this pipeline?

| Claim in the thesis | Depends on | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shorelines for 1990–2025 were digitised from satellite images (Ch. III–IV) | A or B | **NOT USABLE as worded** | Product A is an automatic edge-pixel mask, not digitising; method text must be rewritten |
| Fig. 4.1 five-year shoreline overlay | B | n/a to A | Compare in Phase 3B; A's masks for 2020/2025 are noisy over water |
| Shoreline masks 1990, 2000, 2010 (A) | A | **USABLE WITH CAVEATS** | Consistent noise level (≈ 2.4–2.7 k px); 30 m, edge band ±1 px |
| Shoreline masks 2020, 2025 (A) | A | **NOT USABLE directly** | 83% of 2025 edge pixels in open water; needs cleaning (Phase 3B) |
| EPR 1990–2025 per pixel (A) | A | **NOT USABLE** | Pixel-distance approximation; driven by mask artefacts; one-pixel resolution ≈ 0.86 m/yr |
| Erosion / accretion areas | A | **NOT USABLE** | Accretion 96 % over open sea |
| Risk raster thresholds (Low <2, Medium 2–5, High >5) | A | **USABLE** | Rule matches Table 3.1 exactly (inclusive 2 and 5) |
| Risk raster as a map (Fig. 4.2) | A | **NOT USABLE** | "Low" includes land and sea; High pixels sit in the river mouth, not on the open coast |
| Locations of Medium/High pixels | A | **USABLE WITH CAVEATS** | Screening hint of hot spots (river-mouth sandbars, Linao spit); not a rate |
| Table 4.2 (mean/min/max EPR, Low/Medium/High ha per barangay) from the CSV | A (CSV) | **NOT USABLE** | 1 km circles around points; NaN/zero rows; Low ≈ circle area |
| "Mean EPR" of a barangay | A | **NOT USABLE** | Average of mostly zero pixels incl. sea |
| Statement that 2000/2010/2020 shorelines informed the analysis | A | **NOT SUPPORTED** | Not used in any rate (script §13–19) |

## 7. What must be decided (Decision Gates #1–#4)

1. **Gate 1 / 2:** Who wrote and ran `Code.docx`, and did any value from the 1 km CSV go into the thesis or defense slides? (The empty Table 4.2 suggests not.)
2. **Gate 3:** Which shoreline set is primary — decided after the Phase 3B comparison.
3. **Gate 4:** May Landsat be re-fetched (own Earth Engine account / open STAC)? **Not possible in the current sandbox**; the students can run `scripts/gee_v2.js` themselves.

Files: tables `outputs/tables/gee_*.csv`; maps `outputs/maps/gee_*.png`.
